notes.text: Kailer Yamamoto is day to day (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Clayton Keller has taken his spot beside Anders Lee and Barrett Hayton.
Nate Schmidt is day to day (upper-body injury), reported after he played in their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
John Marino is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and has missed the last 8 games. He is a top-pair defenseman.

Parker Wotherspoon is on injured reserve and has missed the last 12 games. Jérémy Lauzon has taken his spot beside Rasmus Andersson. That pair has had 36% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 130:24 together, down from 54% with Wotherspoon.

stakes: The Mammoth go in second in the Central with 21 points, the Golden Knights second in the Pacific with 24 points.

story.head: A rematch of last spring’s first round
paras: The Golden Knights have won two in a row, while the Mammoth (10-6-1) lost 5-4 in overtime to Montréal on Thursday. Going in, the Mammoth are second in the Central (tied for ninth in the NHL) and the Knights second in the Pacific (fifth).

The Mammoth have played better than their record (.618) says: their chances are worth about .730, and their goaltending has held them back. The Golden Knights’ record (.667) is about what their chances are worth.

The Mammoth roll their lines more evenly than anyone (1st), rarely get pinned in their own end (1st) and let the point shots come and guard the net (1st). As for the Golden Knights, they draw more penalties than they take (1st), have one of the league’s best penalty kills (2nd) and keep dangerous shots away (2nd). Something has to give when the Mammoth’s shooting runs into the Golden Knights’ defense, and the Golden Knights’ power play (4th) could do real damage against the Mammoth’s penalty kill (22nd).

Clayton Keller (4 G / 18 A / 22 P in 17 GP) leads the Mammoth in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Logan Cooley (11 G / 10 A / 21 P in 17 GP) has a team-high eleven goals, tied for sixth in the NHL, with ten points in his last five games and eight goals in nine games against Vegas since 2023-24. Jack Eichel (7 G / 16 A / 23 P in 18 GP) leads the Golden Knights in scoring and is tied for ninth in the NHL, and Mark Stone (10 G / 9 A / 19 P in 18 GP) has a team-high ten goals, tied for tenth in the NHL.

Sebastian Cossa (4-1-1 / .872 SV% in 6 GS) will likely start for Utah. Vegas has two options in net: Carter Hart (5-3-2 / .900 SV% in 10 GS) and Adin Hill (6-2-0 / .895 SV% in 8 GS). They have split the last ten starts, and Hart got the last one on Thursday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
At home, Ryan Craig likes to send Barbashev, Karlsson and Marner out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Keller, Hayton and Lee.

items.text: First meeting since the Golden Knights beat the Mammoth in six games in last spring’s first round, two of them in overtime.

The Mammoth are newly without Kailer Yamamoto and Nate Schmidt, and have been without John Marino since Oct 17. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, no team is missing more right now.
The Golden Knights have been without Parker Wotherspoon since Oct 10.
Logan Cooley has eleven goals on chances worth about 6.2 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
